mainTopic: Cases of doubtful lineage: mixed-up babies and חליצה, רבי מאיר's 'five nations', a son selling his slave father for a כתובה, and the משנה on mixed-up babies for יבום and תרומה
overview: This amud brings several cases about unusual family situations. First a ברייתא shows how a man might do חליצה with a woman who could be his mother, sister or daughter. This happens because babies born 'in hiding' got mixed up, so יבום is impossible and he does חליצה with every woman who might be his יבמה. Next, רבי מאיר shows how one couple, a slave and a maidservant, can have children of five different statuses: גר, גוי, עבד, ממזר and ישראל. The גמרא says the point is that the child of a גוי or עבד with a Jewish woman is a ממזר. Another ברייתא describes a son who sells his own slave father to pay his mother's כתובה. The גמרא explains that it follows רבי מאיר, who holds that מטלטלין are tied up for a כתובה, or else it teaches that a slave counts like קרקע. Then a new משנה rules on יבום and חליצה when a woman's baby got mixed up with her daughter-in-law's baby. Finally, the משנה starts a case of a כהנת's baby mixed up with her שפחה's baby: both eat תרומה but receive one share. This case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Three surprising cases of doubtful חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that there are cases where a man does חליצה with his mother, his sister or his daughter because of a ספק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: sometimes a man does חליצה with his mother because of a doubt, with his sister because of a doubt, or with his daughter because of a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that lists three strange cases. The next steps will explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a man could never be the יבם of his own mother, sister or daughter. The key word is מספק: the חליצה happens only because we are unsure who is who. The ברייתא gives the headline first and explains it afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Performs חליצה, the ceremony that frees a יבמה from her brother-in-law
Because of a doubt
There is (a case where)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying a man is ever truly the יבם of his own mother, sister or daughter. He does חליצה only because we don't know which woman is the relative and which is his real יבמה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There is one who performs חליצה with his mother due to doubt,
with his sister due to doubt,
with his daughter due to doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יֵשׁ חוֹלֵץ לְאִמּוֹ מִסָּפֵק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of a ספק, a man may have to do חליצה with a woman who might be his mother, sister or daughter.

steps.title: How a man does חליצה with his mother out of doubt
steps.stepSummary: Two women each have a known son, then each gives birth to another son in hiding and those babies get mixed up. The known sons marry each other's mothers and die childless, so each mixed-up son does חליצה with both widows, and one of them is his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? A man's mother and another woman each had a son. Then they each gave birth to another son in hiding, and the babies got mixed up. The known son of one woman married the mother of the other known son, and the other known son married the first one's mother. Both husbands died without children. Each of the mixed-up sons does חליצה with both women. So it turns out that each one does חליצה with his own mother because of a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the first case: how a man ends up doing חליצה with his mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The babies born 'in hiding' got mixed up, so neither knows which woman is his mother. Each widow could be his יבמה or his mother. יבום is impossible because she might be his mother, so he does חליצה with both, and one of those חליצות is with his own mother.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces an explanation of a case)
In hiding, so the babies got mixed up and nobody knows whose child is whose
With both of them
It turns out

phrases.english: How so?
His mother and another woman,
and they had two sons,
and they then gave birth to two more sons in hiding,
and the son of this woman came
and married the mother of that one,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְנָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ נָשָׂא אִמּוֹ שֶׁל זֶה,
phrases.english: and the son of that woman married the mother of this one,
and they died without children —
this one performs חליצה with both of them,
phrases.notes: This is one of the two mixed-up sons born in hiding.

phrases.english: and that one performs חליצה with both of them.
It turns out that each and every one
performs חליצה with his mother due to doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the three cases stated in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each mixed-up son does חליצה with both widows, so one of his חליצות is with his own mother.

steps.title: How a man does חליצה with his sister out of doubt
steps.stepSummary: A man's mother and another woman give birth to two daughters in hiding, and the girls get mixed up. Brothers from a different mother marry the girls and die childless, so he does חליצה with both, and one may be his sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: With his sister because of a doubt, how so? His mother and another woman each gave birth to a girl in hiding, and the girls got mixed up. Their brothers from a different mother married them and died without children. He does חליצה with both of them. So it turns out he does חליצה with his sister because of a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the second case: how a man ends up doing חליצה with his sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two baby girls were mixed up, so nobody knows which one is his sister. Each widow might be his sister, so יבום is impossible, and he must do חליצה with both. That means one of the women he does חליצה with may be his own sister.

keyTerms.meaning: Girls, females
Their brothers
Not from that same mother; same father, different mother
With his sister

phrases.english: With his sister due to doubt, how so?
His mother and another woman
who gave birth to two girls in hiding,
and their brothers, not from that same mother, came
and married them,
and they died without children —
he performs חליצה with both of them,
it turns out he performs חליצה with his sister due to doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second case from step 1, using the same 'born in hiding' setup as step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the girls are mixed up, he does חליצה with both widows, so one may be his sister.

steps.title: How a man does חליצה with his daughter out of doubt
steps.stepSummary: A man's wife and another woman give birth to two daughters in hiding, and the girls get mixed up. Brothers marry them and die childless, so each father does חליצה with a woman who might be his own daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: With his daughter because of a doubt, how so? His wife and another woman each gave birth to a girl in hiding, and the girls got mixed up. Brothers married them and died without children. This man does חליצה with his daughter because of a doubt, and that man does חליצה with his daughter because of a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the third and final case: how a man ends up doing חליצה with his daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the mix-up is between two baby girls of two different fathers. Neither father knows which girl is really his. When the girls are widowed and each father must do חליצה, any widow he does חליצה with might be his own daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife
With his daughter
This one... and that one (both fathers)

steps.whatToRemember: All three cases work the same way: babies born 'in hiding' get mixed up, יבום becomes impossible because she might be a close relative, so the man does חליצה with every woman who might be his יבמה, even though one may be his mother, sister or daughter.

phrases.english: With his daughter due to doubt, how so?
His wife and another woman
who gave birth to two girls in hiding,
and their brothers came and married them,
phrases.notes: 'Their brothers' here means the brothers of the two fathers, the men who will later need חליצה.

phrases.english: and they died without children —
this one performs חליצה with his daughter due to doubt,
and that one performs חליצה with his daughter due to doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third and last case from step 1, completing the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When daughters of two fathers are mixed up, each father does חליצה with a widow who may be his own daughter.

steps.title: One couple can have children of five nations
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר states that a man and a woman can sometimes have children who belong to five different categories of lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר used to say: a man and a woman can sometimes have children of five different 'nations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא from רבי מאיר with a surprising claim. It is setting up the case that will explain it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Five nations' does not mean five countries. It means five different legal statuses. The same two parents can have five children who are each a different status, depending on what happened to the parents between births.

keyTerms.meaning: Nations; here, categories of lineage or status
They give birth to, they bear children

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir used to say:
A man and a woman sometimes have children
of five nations.
phrases.notes: He means five different family statuses, not five countries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the earlier ברייתא about unusual family situations, with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One couple can have children of five different lineage statuses.

steps.title: How the five statuses come about
steps.stepSummary: A slave couple's children become a גר, a גוי, an עבד, a ממזר and a ישראל, depending on what changed for the parents before each birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? A Jew buys a non-Jewish slave and maidservant who already have two sons. One son converts, so one is a גר and one a גוי. The master does טבילה for the parents as slaves, and they have a child: now there is also an עבד. He frees the maidservant, and the slave is with her: that child is a ממזר. He frees both and marries them to each other: that child is a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains רבי מאיר's claim step by step, adding one new child with a new status each time the parents' status changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each child's status follows the parents' status at that moment. Before the master's טבילה the parents are גוים, so the older sons are a גוי (and a גר once he converts). After the טבילה they are slaves, so their child is an עבד. Once only the mother is freed, she is a Jewish woman with a slave, and the ברייתא calls that child a ממזר. Once both are free and Jewish, their child is a regular ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism
A non-Jew
A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew
He immersed them to give them the status of slaves
He freed (a slave), which makes the slave a full Jew
A child of a forbidden union, who may not marry a regular Jew

steps.confusionAlert: The parents are the same two people the whole time. Only their status changes, and that is why each new child has a different status.

phrases.english: How so?

phrases.aramaic: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלָּקַח עֶבֶד וְשִׁפְחָה מִן הַשּׁוּק,
phrases.english: A Jew who bought a slave and a maidservant from the market,
and they already had two sons,
and one of the sons converted —
it turns out that one is a convert and one is a gentile.
He immersed the parents to make them slaves
and they were together with each other and had a child,
so here we have a convert, a gentile and a slave.
He freed the maidservant
and the slave was with her and they had a child,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי כָּאן גֵּר וְגוֹי וְעֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר.
phrases.english: so here we have a convert, a gentile, a slave and a mamzer.
He freed both of them and married them to each other —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי כָּאן גֵּר וְגוֹי וְעֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר וְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: so here we have a convert, a gentile, a slave, a mamzer and a Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלָּקַח עֶבֶד וְשִׁפְחָה מִן הַשּׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case behind רבי מאיר's statement in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each child takes the status the parents had at the time: גוי/גר, then עבד, then ממזר, then ישראל.

steps.title: What is this case really teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the point of רבי מאיר's case is, and answers that a child of a גוי or עבד with a Jewish woman is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching us? That when a גוי or an עבד is with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what new law is hidden inside the long story, and then answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the five statuses are obvious. The one real חידוש is the fourth child: a freed maidservant (now Jewish) with a slave produces a ממזר. From this the גמרא pulls a general rule for both a גוי and an עבד with a Jewish woman.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (asking for the new point)
A Jewish woman
The child, the offspring

steps.whatToRemember: The lesson of רבי מאיר's 'five nations' case is that the child of a גוי or עבד with a Jewish woman is a ממזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a strange story into a practical rule about lineage and who may marry whom.

phrases.english: What is this teaching us?

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: That a gentile or a slave who is with a Jewish woman,
the child is a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the legal point of the case in step 6 and identifies it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law the ברייתא of the five nations is teaching.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: That a child of a גוי or עבד with a Jewish woman is a ממזר.

steps.title: A son can sell his father to pay his mother's marriage contract
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא states that there is a case where a son sells his own father to collect his mother's כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: there is a case where a man sells his father to collect his mother's כתובה for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second strange ברייתא and states its surprising claim. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling your own father sounds impossible, so the ברייתא grabs our attention. The next step shows the exact case where this can happen.

keyTerms.meaning: Sells his father
To collect (a debt) for someone
Marriage contract; money owed to a wife

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There is a case where one sells his father
to collect his mother's marriage contract for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יֵשׁ מוֹכֵר אֶת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate ברייתא about another unusual family situation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a case where a son sells his father to pay his mother's כתובה.

steps.title: How a son ends up selling his father
steps.stepSummary: A master frees and marries a slave woman, then gives all his property to her son; that property includes the son's father, the slave, who can be sold to pay her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? A Jew bought a slave and a maidservant who had a son. He freed the maidservant and married her, and then wrote all his property over to her son. So the son may end up selling his father to collect his mother's כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the case behind the surprising claim of step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son's father is still a slave, so he is part of the master's property. When the master writes all his property to the son, the son now owns his own father. Since the mother, as the master's wife, is owed her כתובה, the son can sell that slave (his father) to pay her.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish maidservant owned by a Jew
He married her
He wrote over (gave) all his property
It turns out

steps.whatToRemember: A slave counts as property, so a son who inherits or is given that property can end up owning, and even selling, his own father.

phrases.english: How so?

phrases.aramaic: יִשְׂרָאֵל לָקַח עֶבֶד וְשִׁפְחָה מִן הַשּׁוּק
phrases.english: A Jew bought a slave and a maidservant from the market
and they had a son.
And he freed the maidservant and married her,
and then he wrote all his property over to her son,
phrases.notes: 'All his property' includes the slave, who is the son's own father.

phrases.english: it turns out that this son sells his father
to collect his mother's marriage contract for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? יִשְׂרָאֵל לָקַח עֶבֶד וְשִׁפְחָה מִן הַשּׁוּק וְלָהֶם בֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case behind the claim in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the master gives all his property to the freed maidservant's son, the son owns his slave father and can sell him to pay his mother's כתובה.

steps.title: What is this ברייתא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point the ברייתא about the son selling his father is trying to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the lesson is behind the strange case from Steps 8-9. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 8-9 described a son who sells his own father, a slave, to pay his mother's כתובה. That is a strange story, so the גמרא wants to know what halachic point is hidden inside it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (asks for the new point)

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from the last two steps, where the son sells his father for his mother's כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the purpose of the case in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What halachic point the case of the son selling his father teaches.

steps.title: First answer: it follows רבי מאיר on movable property
steps.stepSummary: The whole ברייתא is רבי מאיר. A slave counts as movable property, and in his view movable property is tied up to pay a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole ברייתא is רבי מאיר. A slave counts as movable property, and movable property is tied up for a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. He holds that a husband's movable property, which includes a slave, is tied up to pay his wife's כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some opinions hold that only land is tied up for a כתובה, not מטלטלין. The ברייתא shows רבי מאיר's view: even a slave, which counts as מטלטלין, can be collected for the כתובה. That is why the son can sell his father.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable property (things that can be carried, not land)
Are tied up (as a guarantee) to pay a debt
The money a husband owes his wife when the marriage ends
The whole of it (the entire ברייתא)

phrases.english: The whole of it is Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: This ברייתא about the son selling his father also follows רבי מאיר, just like the 'five nations' one in Step 5.

phrases.english: and a slave counts as movable property,
and movable property is tied up for a marriage contract.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds that movable property, including a slave, is tied up for a כתובה.

steps.title: Second answer: a slave counts like land
steps.stepSummary: Or, the ברייתא teaches that a slave is treated like land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say it is teaching us this: a slave is like land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. The ברייתא is teaching that a slave has the status of קרקע (land).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a slave counts like land, the ברייתא no longer depends on רבי מאיר's special view about מטלטלין. Land is tied up for a כתובה in everyone's opinion, so the son selling his father to pay the כתובה works for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Land / real estate
Is like, is compared to

steps.whatToRemember: The son-sells-father ברייתא is about whether a slave can be collected for a כתובה. Either it follows רבי מאיר (מטלטלין are tied up), or it teaches that a slave counts like קרקע.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
it is teaching us this:
a slave is like land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of Step 10, so the ברייתא no longer has to follow only רבי מאיר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A slave has the status of land, so he is tied up for a כתובה in everyone's opinion.

steps.title: Mixed-up babies: the daughter-in-law's sons may only do חליצה
steps.stepSummary: A woman's baby got mixed up with her daughter-in-law's baby. The two grew up, married and died. The daughter-in-law's sons do חליצה with the widows but not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman's baby got mixed up with her daughter-in-law's baby. The mixed-up babies grew up, married women, and died. The daughter-in-law's sons do חליצה and not יבום, because each widow might be his brother's wife or might be his father's brother's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Two babies got mixed up: one is the grandmother's son and one is her grandson. The משנה rules that the daughter-in-law's other sons can only do חליצה with these men's widows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a son of the daughter-in-law, each dead man is either his brother or his uncle (his father's brother). A brother's widow is a יבמה, but an uncle's wife is forbidden to him. Since we are not sure which, he cannot marry her, but he does חליצה in case she is his brother's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
The mixed-up ones (the babies who got mixed up)
Daughter-in-law
They do חליצה (the ceremony that releases a יבמה)
They do יבום (marry the dead brother's widow)
His father's brother's wife (his aunt by marriage), who is forbidden to him

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the family straight. The 'elder woman' (זקנה) is the grandmother. The כלה is married to the grandmother's son. So one mixed baby is an uncle and the other is his nephew.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A woman whose baby got mixed up
with her daughter-in-law's baby,
the mixed-up ones grew up
and married women, and died —
the daughter-in-law's sons do חליצה
but do not do יבום,
because she might be his brother's wife,
or might be his father's brother's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the mixed-up men die, the daughter-in-law's certain sons do חליצה but not יבום, because each widow may be forbidden to them as an uncle's wife.

steps.title: The grandmother's sons may do חליצה or יבום
steps.stepSummary: The grandmother's sons may either do חליצה or יבום, because each widow is either a brother's wife or a nephew's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The elder woman's sons either do חליצה or do יבום, because each widow might be his brother's wife or his brother's son's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now rules for the grandmother's sons, whose identity is certain. With the mixed-up men's widows, they may do either חליצה or יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a son of the grandmother, each dead man is either his brother or his nephew. A brother's widow is his יבמה, and a nephew's wife is permitted to him. Either way she is not forbidden, so יבום is also possible.

keyTerms.meaning: The elder woman (the grandmother / mother-in-law)
His brother's son's wife (his nephew's wife), who is permitted to him

phrases.english: The elder woman's sons
either do חליצה or do יבום,
because she might be his brother's wife
phrases.notes: Some versions add the word in square brackets; others leave it out.

phrases.english: or his brother's son's wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי הַזְּקֵנָה אוֹ חוֹלְצִין אוֹ מְיַיבְּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting rule for the other family line in the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The grandmother's certain sons may do either חליצה or יבום, since neither possibility makes the widow forbidden to them.

steps.title: Reverse case: mixed-up men with the grandmother's sons' widows
steps.stepSummary: If the certain brothers died instead, the mixed-up men may only do חליצה with the widows of the grandmother's sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ones with certain identity died, the mixed-up men do חליצה but not יבום with the widows of the elder woman's sons, because each widow might be his brother's wife or his father's brother's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the case. Now the brothers whose identity is certain died, and the mixed-up men are left alive. With the grandmother's sons' widows, the mixed-up men can only do חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mixed-up man might be the grandmother's son, so the dead man is his brother. Or he might be the grandson, so the dead man is his uncle, whose wife is forbidden to him. Because of that doubt, only חליצה is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The ones whose identity is certain (not mixed up)

phrases.english: If the ones with certain identity died,
the mixed-up ones, for the elder woman's sons,
do חליצה but not יבום,
because she might be his brother's wife
or his father's brother's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the case of Steps 13-14: now the certain brothers die and the mixed-up men remain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the widows of the grandmother's sons, the mixed-up men do only חליצה, since she may be an uncle's wife to them.

steps.title: Mixed-up men with the daughter-in-law's sons' widows
steps.stepSummary: With the daughter-in-law's sons' widows, one mixed-up man does חליצה and the other does יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the daughter-in-law's sons: one does חליצה and one does יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the reverse case. With the widows of the daughter-in-law's sons, one mixed-up man does חליצה and the other does יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a mixed-up man, the dead son of the daughter-in-law is either his brother or his nephew. A nephew's wife is permitted, so יבום is never forbidden here. Still, one of them does חליצה in case she is his brother's wife. Then the other may do יבום, since she is either his brother's wife or his nephew's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: One does חליצה and one does יבום

steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה depends on one question: is the dead man possibly an uncle of the living man? If yes, the widow might be forbidden, so only חליצה. If the worst case is a nephew's wife, which is permitted, יבום can happen.

phrases.english: For the daughter-in-law's sons —
phrases.notes: He means the widows of the daughter-in-law's certain sons, who died.

phrases.english: one does חליצה, and one does יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִבְנֵי הַכַּלָּה אֶחָד חוֹלֵץ וְאֶחָד מְיַיבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reverse case by ruling on the other family's widows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the daughter-in-law's sons' widows, one mixed-up man does חליצה in case she is his brother's wife, and the other does יבום, since she is permitted to him either way.

steps.title: A priestess's baby mixed up with her maidservant's baby
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that two mixed-up babies, one the son of a כהנת and one the son of her שפחה, both eat תרומה but receive only one share at the granary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a כהנת's baby got mixed up with her maidservant's baby, both of them may eat תרומה, and together they receive one share at the threshing floor.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with another mixed-up-babies case. This time one baby is a כהן and the other is a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We don't know which child is the כהן and which is the slave. That doesn't matter for eating תרומה, because a כהן eats it and a slave owned by a כהן also eats it. But when תרומה is handed out at the granary, the pair gets just one share together, not two.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman from a כהן's family; here, the mother of the כהן baby
A non-Jewish maidservant (female slave)
Got mixed up, so no one knows which is which
The holy portion of produce given to כהנים, which only they and their household may eat
The threshing floor (granary), where תרומה was handed out

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the slave child eats תרומה only because he might be the כהן. Even if he really is the slave, he still eats, because a כהן's slave is allowed to eat תרומה.

phrases.english: A priestess whose baby got mixed up
with her maidservant's baby
these may eat תרומה
phrases.notes: Either way they're covered: one is a כהן, and the other is a כהן's slave.

phrases.english: and they receive one share at the threshing floor,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the mixed-up babies of a woman and her daughter-in-law (יבום and חליצה) to a new mixed-up case involving a כהן and a slave (תרומה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both mixed-up children eat תרומה, but they receive only one share together at the granary.
